args.name: Make and test vine cordage
args.function: Provide a learnable way to turn owned vine material into a real reusable binding, if physically supported, and perform a bounded load test that measures whether it holds. The problem is that visible vines alone establish neither binding feasibility nor strength.
args.conditions: Sol is beside the observed forest-vine-2 source. Its visible stock was 12 at tick 61. No vine strength, processing method or personal cordage mastery is established. Use only actually owned material and observed conditions; report unsupported effects rather than granting them.
args.inputs: Owned vine material if gathering succeeds; any additional required inputs must be identified, not assumed available.
args.costs: Method, learning time, work and material requirements are unknown; specify actual costs and interruption rules.
args.effects: If supported, produce a persistent physical binding and an evidence-based load-test result. Do not infer shelter, tool quality, safety, comfort or benefits merely from requesting or learning.

candidates.function: Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.

candidates.function: Arrange owned loose moss as a small ground patch, inspect it, try one ordinary rest on it, or take back what remains; resume or cancel unfinished arranging.
candidates.costs: Arrange: inputStackId of owned moss, quantity in 0.1 steps (default 0.5) and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy in reach. Trial-rest: stand on a completed, unoccupied patch; one ordinary rest round. Remove: the arranger only, unoccupied patch, one round and one energy.
candidates.effects: A completed patch holds the reserved material in a 0.25-radius footprint used only for occupancy and drawing; no thickness, coverage, body fit, warmth, insulation or comfort is inferred. Trial-rest runs the existing rest action unchanged and records energy before and after; the patch is not a registered facility, so it adds no recovery bonus. Inspect records visible placement, remaining quantity, occupancy and tests as a personal unverified record. Remove returns the remaining material as an owned stack at the site and deletes the patch; pickup stays a separate action. Cancel releases reserved material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward, regrowth, repair or top-up.

candidates.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
candidates.costs: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
candidates.effects: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

candidates.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
candidates.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
candidates.effects: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

candidates.function: Place one or two whole units of an owned food on the ground as a paired exposure trial, inspect their quantity and decay, end the observation or retrieve what remains.
candidates.costs: Start: inputStackId of an owned, unspoiled, nontoxic food, quantity 1 or 2 whole units (default 2), and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: target trial in reach, one round and 0.2 energy. Retrieve: operator only, one round and one energy. Cancel of an exposed trial ends observation at no cost. No supports, tools, water or fuel are used or granted.
candidates.effects: Completed setup places the samples at two ground positions 0.2 apart under the same ambient conditions; with one unit there is no matched control. No food moisture, drying or preservation model exists in this world: both samples keep the existing decay rules, so no treatment difference, preserved status, safety certification or extended lifetime is produced. The trial records rounds exposed and marks a 10-round observation checkpoint; ageing continues while unattended and after the checkpoint. Inspect records sample quantity and decay as a personal unverified record. Retrieve returns only the remaining material, never a replacement. Setup interruption keeps paid work; cancel releases reserved food once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for starting, inspecting or retrieving.

candidates.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
candidates.costs: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
candidates.effects: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

candidates.function: Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
candidates.costs: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
candidates.effects: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

candidates.function: Check a site and owned branches for a freestanding branch wind screen and report what the world cannot yet support; no screen can currently be built.
candidates.costs: Build with x/y and orientation (degrees) checks the 2 m x 1 m footprint and 1 m x 1 m lee space for reach, bounds, ordinary soil and occupancy, and counts owned branch units against the 12 required, then fails without spending anything. Other modes fail at no cost because no barrier can exist.
candidates.effects: Currently unsupported: branch records carry no length or diameter, so stakes and woven members cannot be qualified, and world wind has strength but no direction, so lee-side protection cannot be computed. No structure, reservation, protection, comfort or reward is produced. A working screen needs a separately decided branch geometry and wind direction model; none is invented here.

packet.access: Search or retrieve only this experiment abilities with control queries. Missing candidates do not prove a function absent. Full implementation facts remain available in the development handoff; never grant inventory or individual mastery. Require actual physical prerequisites.
